function: Gradient-based meta-learning networks jointly optimize transmit and receive beamformers, UL power, and MA positions, maximizing echo SINR at BS R under QoS constraints (p. 1, p. 4)
system: FD ISAC BS with movable transmit/receive antennas, receiving BS R with MAs, DL/UL users with one fixed antenna, one target; no RIS; antenna counts and band not stated (p. 1, 5)
method: Gradient-based meta-learning: neural sub-networks take objective gradients and output variable updates; trained with Adam on a label-free meta-loss (objective plus constraint penalties), no pre-training (p. 4)
data_channel: Custom field-response-vector channel model per [3], simulated; parameters follow [4]; averaged over 150 Monte Carlo runs; no standard model or dataset (p. 2, p. 5)
test_conditions: No separate training and test conditions described; results swept over BS power, SI level, and DL/UL rate thresholds, averaged over 150 Monte Carlo runs (p. 5)
baselines: fmincon solver (non-learned); FD-ISAC with MAs only at FD BS; FD-ISAC with FPAs at both BSs; no earlier learned method compared (p. 5)
metrics: SINR of reflected echo at BS R versus BS power, SI level, and DL/UL rate thresholds; objective convergence; 99% of fmincon optimum (p. 5)
q1_support: p. 2: "we adopt the field response channel model for all communication links" - custom field-response simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "the results are averaged over 150 Monte Carlo iterations" - only sweeps of BS power, SI, and rate thresholds (Figs. 2-3); no unseen scenario, transfer, or fine-tuning test is stated.
q3_support: p. 5: "This benchmark leverages a predefined MATLAB solver" - fmincon is the only non-learned baseline; the FPA benchmarks are system variants, and no earlier learned method or standard learning algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "thus reducing the complexity" - qualitative claim only (attributed to [9]); no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime is reported anywhere.
q5_support: p. 5: "The model parameters adopted in this work follow [4]" - setup refers to an earlier paper; simulated data, no code or data link or DOI, no public dataset or measurement.
notes: PDF is the arXiv preprint 2510.01437v1 (1 Oct 2025), titled Meta-Learning-Driven Resource Optimization in Full-Duplex ISAC with Movable Antennas; the file does not print the DOI, so the DOI-to-title match cannot be checked from it. Included as a learned optimizer: sub-networks trained with Adam on a meta-loss (p. 4-5), but with no pre-training phase (p. 4), so training looks online per problem; reviewer to confirm it counts as learned and not as an iterative optimization algorithm. Antenna counts, band, and number of users are not given (parameters follow [4]); channels are scalar per user (p. 2), so users have one antenna.
